alignments.note: Conjunction rendered by the connective *Yea*, which rule 14's open list includes.
Imperative with the subject pronoun the ASV writes after it, under rule 17.
Absolute noun, the head of the English possessive expression.

The ASV writes the possessive `לְ`'s relation inside the following word as an English genitive, so one rendering carries both the relation and the lexeme and the two morphemes share a unit under rules 30 and 49, headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Pronominal suffix realized by the possessive *thy*, which stands at the left edge because an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor (rule 29).
Subject of the verbless clause, taking only its own English while the copula joins the prepositional predicate under rules 20 and 49.
Preposition heading the predicate of a verbless clause; the construction-supplied copula joins it and the unit heads on the preposition under rule 49.
Proper name, object of the prepositional predicate.

review_notes: `בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ` → *thy children's children*: the `לְ` has no English word of its own and its relation is written inside the genitive *children's*, so it fuses with `בָנֶיךָ`'s noun under rule 49's closing sentence. The competing reading would mark the `לְ` `unrepresented` under rule 40; that was set aside because the genitive marker is written on a word that would otherwise stand bare.

The ASV margin offers *Or, And peace upon Israel* for the last colon. It was read and set aside under rule 38: the printed text's *Peace be upon Israel* governs, so the copula goes to the `עַל` heading the prepositional predicate.
